title: Saving for College with Compound Interest
learningObjectives: Understand how time and compound interest can increase savings
Understand the value of starting early to save for post-secondary education

evidence.quote: Compound interest is when you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.

explanations.text: Compound interest means you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you have already earned, so starting early helps savings grow.

evidence.quote: So let's say you invest $1,000 (your principal) and it earns 5 percent (interest rate) once a year (the compounding frequency).
The second year, you would have $1,102.50.

explanations.text: For example, a $1,000 principal at 5 percent compounded once a year grows to $1,102.50 after two years.

evidence.quote: Interest can be compounded annually (once each year), semi-annually (twice each year), monthly, or daily.
Increasing the compounding frequency or your interest rate or adding to your principal can help your savings grow even faster.

explanations.text: Interest can be compounded annually, semi-annually, monthly, or daily, and increasing frequency, rate, or principal can help savings grow even faster.
